summary: Feed s127_double is degraded: IDS drops 4.2% oversize frames (>1518B) and cannot inspect 28.6% ERSPAN-tunneled traffic, creating detection blind spots.

findings.root_cause: Source network uses jumbo frames up to 8108 bytes but IDS tool port is standard 1518B MTU and packet broker forwards them unchanged without slicing or MTU handling.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC silently drops 142/3381 frames (4.2%) exceeding 1518B, so IDS misses full flows and payload for large transfers, reducing detection coverage for attacks using large packets.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs full payload and cannot process truncated frames; increasing tool port MTU to 9216 (or at least 8108) or enabling jumbo support on broker egress prevents drops without slicing payload needed for IDS signatures.

findings.root_cause: 28.6% of traffic arrives encapsulated in ERSPAN (968/3381 frames) and packet broker is not stripping the tunnel header before delivery to IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS sees only outer ERSPAN headers and cannot parse inner original L2-L7 headers/payload, so 28.6% of traffic is opaque to IDS signatures and anomaly detection.

recommended_fix.why: Stripping ERSPAN at the packet broker exposes inner packets to the IDS, restoring visibility without requiring IDS to support tunnel decapsulation.
